text:
mike: Quick API-contract question — if we change the account default model (default_model) how do we guarantee backward compatibility for existing clients that don't explicitly pin a version?

sana: Good one. Short answer: unpinned requests follow the new default. Pinned requests (via Model-Version header or model_version param) keep returning the pinned variant until that exact variant is removed.

mike: OK — what happens if we remove a pinned variant entirely? auto-fallback or error? we've had customers rely on exact behavior.

devon: We discussed auto-fallback earlier. Plan was: if the exact pinned artifact is gone, try a same-family compatible fallback (patch/minor). If none found, return 409 + explanatory message. Fallback only within semver-compatible family.

priya: +1 on conservative approach. Also we should add a clear response shape so clients can programmatically detect a pin failure. e.g.

```http
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "error": "pinned_model_unavailable",
  "message": "Requested model version 'redwood-model@1.2.0' was removed. No compatible fallback found.",
  "recommended_action": "pin to a supported variant or remove model pin to use account default",
  "compatible_versions": []
}
```

lia: +1. Also include an optional header so SDKs can surface a warning: `X-Model-Warning: pinned model unavailable; no compatible fallback`. That helps clients without parsing body.

mike: Sounds good. What about deprecation timelines / comms? we need a formal rule so product/legal know what to promise.

sana: Proposal:
- Minor/patch substitutions (non-breaking perf/ops only): 30 days notice via console banner + email to admin contact.
- Major changes that affect output shape or tokenizer: 90 days notice, plus migration doc and deprecation flag in the Console.
- Removal of a model variant (i.e., pinned version deletion): 60 days notice and a managed migration window where we offer automated fallback for compatible minors.

devon: And for Hosted API customers with Dedicated/Private tiers we should make it opt-in to apply automatic remapping. For Dedicated we won't auto-remap without customer approval.

priya: We should also update SDKs to:
1) send `Model-Version` header when user pins in client config
2) surface a structured warning if response has `error: pinned_model_unavailable`
3) log a telemetry event `pin_unavailable` so we can detect affected customers early

mike: Good checklist. Can someone put together a short engineering playbook for a breaking-change rollout? steps + who pings customers + console banner copy?

lia: I'll draft a runbook. Minimal steps:
- Create internal RFC + support KB (PR)
- Add deprecation flag + banner in Console (frontend)
- SDK patch with warning + header behavior
- Add compatibility test in CI (sample prompts + eval)
- Send staged email to admin contacts @ 60/30/7 days
- Monitor `pin_unavailable` telemetry and open a migration ticket for any customer > 5% error rate

deploy-bot: deploy webapp/staging @ 1764125000 — Console banner experiment enabled for 5% of orgs.

devon: One more thing — we need an API for querying available variants so clients can proactively check before pinning. e.g. GET /models/<family>/versions -> returns list with stability tags and deprecation_date.

sana: Yup. Expose `deprecated_until` and `removal_date` fields in that response so UI/SDK can warn early. Also add `compatibility_range` metadata for each version.

mike: Perfect. Action items:
- lia: runbook + banner copy (ETA end of week)
- devon: models API schema + backend changes (ETA next sprint)
- priya: SDK warning + telemetry PR (ETA 3 days)
- sana: finalize comms timeline with support (ETA 2 days)

mike: Thanks — if anyone has objections to the 60/90/30 split speak up now, otherwise we'll lock and add to the eng playbook.

sana: No objections from me.

devon: n/a from infra side.

priya: all good. I'll start the SDK patch.

lia: I'll drop a draft in #eng-docs when ready.

mike: Great. Closing thread — we can follow up in the RFC. :thumbsup:
